title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'Longue Marche' continuation, which studies group schemes over a base S_0. Writing Γ(...) for groups of sections, the objects are subgroups of a group G_{ρ,σ} attached to two torsion elements ρ and σ. The notation looks like the genus-0/genus-1 Teichmüller situation (an SL_2(Z)-like configuration), with σ of order 4 (L_σ ≅ (Z/4Z)_{S_0} on the next page) and ρ presumably of order 6. This identification is my inference. N_ρ is the normalizer-type group of the cyclic subgroup L_ρ. It is an extension 1 → L_ρ → N_ρ → D_12^* → 1, with χ_ρ: N_ρ → D_12^* the quotient map. D_12^* is a finite 'dihedral-type' group of order 12 (my inference). It carries characters ε_2, ε_3 with values in μ = {±1}. Inside it sit index-2 subgroups D_12^{*'} = ker ε_1 (?), D_12^{*''} = ker ε_2 and D_12^{*'''} = ker(ε_2 ε_3), and D_12^{*°} = D' ∩ D''.

Previous page. Grothendieck shows that N_ρ^{'''} = (μτ')_{S_0} · (N_ρ^{⇆})° maps isomorphically onto D_12^{*'''} via χ_ρ (formula 169).

This page.
1. He concludes that N_ρ^{'''} is a partial section of the extension N_ρ → D_12^*, i.e. a splitting over the index-2 subgroup D_12^{*'''}.
2. To cover all of D_12^*, he sets Z_ρ^! = Z_ρ^{0φ} × μ_{S_0}, where μ = {1,−1} is the central ±1 inside L_ρ. He notes that Z^! is normalized by τ'.
3. He defines N_ρ^? = (μ_{τ'})_{S_0} · Z_ρ^! ⊂ N_ρ. Then Z_ρ^{0φ} has index 2 in Z^! and index 4 in N^?.
4. Corollary 4: there is an exact sequence 1 → μ_{S_0} → N_ρ^? → D_12^* → 1, with μ_{S_0} = μ_ρ. So N_ρ^? is a 'bi-section' of the extension N_ρ of D_12^* by L_ρ. It is a subgroup surjecting onto the quotient with kernel exactly the order-2 subgroup μ ⊂ L_ρ, i.e. a splitting up to ±1. Equivalently, the class of the extension in H^2(D_12^*, L_ρ) does not vanish (or at least is not shown to vanish) but comes from μ_2 ⊂ L_ρ.
5. He ends with a programme: develop the diagram of remarkable subgroups of N_ρ, modelled on diagram (38) of p. 622. The next page carries out the parallel analysis for N_σ, where a genuine splitting D_12^* ↪ N_σ^S exists.

Purpose. The aim is to understand fully the normalizers of the finite cyclic 'rotation' subgroups (orders 6 and 4) and their decomposition into semidirect or almost-semidirect products. This is the bookkeeping needed for the torsion and local-monodromy part of a Galois–Teichmüller / Longue Marche type description.
errors: Possible internal tension in the index counts. With Z^{0φ} of index 4 in N^? and N^?/μ ≅ D_12^*, the image of Z^{0φ} in D_12^* would have index 2 (if Z^{0φ} ∩ μ = 1). That should be consistent with the earlier identification of N''' with D_12^{*'''}, but the page does not make it explicit.
The claim that Z^! is normalized by τ' is asserted without proof on this page (presumably it follows from Corollaries 1–2 of the previous page).
Notation is admittedly unstable: the previous page's margin says 'il faudrait changer notation'. Symbols such as N^{'''φ} vs N'''(-ς) and N^? are provisional.

ideas.what: Partial splitting of the extension N_ρ → D_12^* over an index-2 subgroup D_12^{*'''}
ideas.modern_name: section of a group extension over a subgroup
ideas.where_published: not in the published La Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know

ideas.what: 'Bi-section': a subgroup N^? mapping onto the quotient D_12^* with kernel μ_2 = {±1} ⊂ L_ρ, i.e. the extension reduced to a central ±1-extension
ideas.modern_name: reduction of an extension class to μ_2 / central extension by ±1 (analogous to binary polyhedral / metaplectic-type lifts)

ideas.what: Programme to draw a lattice of remarkable subgroups of the normalizer N_ρ, analogous to diagram (38) of p. 622
ideas.modern_name: subgroup lattice of normalizers of torsion subgroups in a Teichmüller/modular-type group

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves undeveloped the full diagram of remarkable subgroups of N_ρ, which was meant to parallel diagram (38) of p. 622. This is a minor bookkeeping thread about normalizers of order-6 torsion.
missed.quote: Il y aurait lieu de développer le diagramme des sous-groupes remarquables de N_ρ, calqué sur le diag. (38) de p. 622.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally relevant. Explicit descriptions of normalizers of torsion in SL_2(Z)/mapping class groups and their profinite or Galois analogues are known. A completed diagram would be a curiosity for Galois–Teichmüller historians, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine finite group-extension bookkeeping (partial sections, a ±1-'bi-section') inside a long technical computation. Nothing on it appears to be a missed result or connection.
transcription_corrections: In the first line, 'sur' before D_12^{*'''} appears struck through or overwritten; the sense is 'section partielle de N_ρ sur D_12^{*'''}'.
In (170), the parenthetical reads '(μ = {1, −1})' fairly clearly.
Under (171), the label '{+on peut introduire+}' is written above a struck 'on pose'.
Under (172), the labels read 'μ_{S_0} ‖dfn μ_ρ' under the first term and an underbrace 'γ_{ρ,σ}' (or Γ_{ρ,σ}) under D_12^*.

In the oblique left margin, a tentative reading is 'NB Il y aurait lieu de faire [de même?] ... D_12^* ... N_ρ ... N_ρ^? ... diagramme ... des sous-groupes ...'. It largely restates the programme at the bottom of the page.
Page number in the lower left: 81.
